notes.A: Paving and burning sky dominate. The flame and basin are clipped.
notes.B: Lamps lead past the flame pedestal into empty paving. The basin is cut off.
notes.C: The basin fills the foreground and makes the flame pedestal look incidental.
notes.D: The storefront and church wall frame the square. The pedestal’s base drops below the frame.
notes.E: The memorial anchors the square. Its pedestal partly hides the basin.
notes.F: The basin and church spire give context. A foreground lamp overlaps the memorial.
notes.G: The skyline locates the memorial in the city. Only the basin’s rim makes the frame.
notes.H: The flame and inscription face the viewer. An oversized foreground lamp crowds the basin.

monument.best: The flame, basin, streetlamps, and storefront read together as a city square beneath a burning sky.
monument.lacks: The square lacks a memorial with a recognizable silhouette. The low stack of stone blocks gets lost against the broad paving and repetitive façades.
monument.fix: Replace the block pedestal with a taller sculpted stone memorial that tapers toward the flame, giving the square a landmark visible from across the plaza.

blind_name.name: Flame monument in a city plaza
blind_name.why: A flame crowns a stepped stone pedestal in a cobbled square lined with streetlamps and brick buildings.
blind_name.odd: The red sky looks like a wall of fire, and the far corner is hard to read.

notes.A: Windowed blocks flank a narrow alley, but an oversized foreground lamp steals attention.
notes.B: A tall corner block meets an open paved area whose far edge disappears into darkness.
notes.C: A lamplit open space meets a curving street, partly hidden by the near stone wall.
notes.D: The road bends around a tall block, with repetitive windows dominating the view.
notes.E: A long avenue runs past a stone tower, then vanishes into a murky distance.
notes.F: A lamp and rough stone wall anchor the corner, but the lamp blocks the junction.
notes.G: Two contrasting façades frame a side street, though the flat frontage dominates.
notes.H: Two streets wrap around a low stone building, while the shadowed background obscures their destinations.

avenue.place: Lamplit city streets under red skies
avenue.best: H shows the streets splitting around the low stone building, with taller blocks and lamps framing both routes.
avenue.lacks: The junction lacks a landmark at street level. Repeated façades and evenly spaced lamps give the eye few clues about where to look or go.
avenue.fix: Give the low stone building a lit entrance facing the fork, with a distinctive marquee visible from both approaches.

blind_name.name: Lamplit city street junction
blind_name.why: Two cobblestone streets meet around a stone building, with glowing streetlamps along the sidewalks.
blind_name.odd: Deep shadows obscure the buildings in the distance.

notes.A: The doorway and narrow street are clear, but the stained glass recedes into a sliver.
notes.B: The window row reads clearly, but the tower fills the foreground and hides the entrance.
notes.C: Shows the tower and window rhythm, but the entrance is out of sight.
notes.D: Shows the tower, doorway, and street corner, but crops much of the stained-glass row.
notes.E: Reveals the gable and walled yard, but the foreground wall hides the church’s base.
notes.F: Shows the windows and doorway clearly, but crops the roof and tower.
notes.G: Shows the stained glass along the street, but the doorway sinks into shadow.
notes.H: Shows the church and its city setting together, though the tower top is cropped.

church_out.best: H shows the pitched roof, stained glass, tower, and doorway together, with enough street to place the church downtown.
church_out.lacks: The church lacks a recognizable entrance. The small wooden door gets lost at the foot of the tower, leaving the repeated windows to carry the whole facade.
church_out.fix: Rebuild the doorway as a recessed pointed-arch stone portal that gives the tower a recognizable entrance from the street.

blind_name.name: Church exterior
blind_name.why: Tall stained-glass windows line the stone wall beside a square tower and wooden door.
blind_name.odd: The dark pavement makes the far side of the street hard to read.

notes.A: The altar, tapestry, and skeletons give it character. A bulky pier crowds the right.
notes.B: A frontal view frames the altar. One broad pew conceals the rows behind it.
notes.C: The reverse view shows pews, banner, and skeletons. The altar is out of frame.
notes.D: Pew rows lead toward the altar. A low overhang makes the nave feel cramped.
notes.E: Tall windows and pew rows frame the sanctuary. The altar sits near the edge.
notes.F: Colored windows and a banner dress the corner. The frame cuts off the pews.
notes.G: Altar steps and side windows locate the view. Close pew ends dominate.
notes.H: Pews, a portrait, and a skeleton show the side wall. The altar disappears.

nave.best: E shows the nave’s height, colored windows, rows of pews, and candlelit altar in one view.
nave.lacks: A clear processional aisle. The unbroken pew rows push circulation to the walls and interrupt the sightline from the back of the nave to the altar.
nave.fix: Split the pew rows down the middle to create a continuous aisle leading straight to the altar steps.

blind_name.name: Chapel nave
blind_name.why: Wooden pews face a raised altar with candles and a religious image, beneath tall stained-glass windows.
blind_name.odd: The ceiling and foreground pews are very dark.

notes.A: The hooded figure looms so close it hides almost the entire crypt.
notes.B: Both figures stand beyond the tomb, whose near side fills the lower frame.
notes.C: The side aisle reveals gore and a skeleton, but the near wall crowds them.
notes.D: Barrels and reliefs read clearly, but the sarcophagus and hooded figure are cropped.
notes.E: Barrels and cobwebs give the tomb context, but the looming skeleton dominates.
notes.F: The hooded figure stands beneath a relief, but the sarcophagus runs off the frame.
notes.G: The carved lid and barrels are clear, but the skeleton is cut in half.
notes.H: The tomb and both figures read clearly, though the bare right wall weakens the composition.

crypt.best: The diagonal view gives the carved sarcophagus depth and shows both figures, burial reliefs, and cobwebs in context.
crypt.lacks: The crypt lacks a sense of ceremony. The low, flat ceiling and repeating reliefs make the sarcophagus feel like furniture.
crypt.fix: Raise a ribbed stone vault directly over the sarcophagus so the room’s architecture draws the eye to the tomb.

blind_name.name: Stone crypt with a sarcophagus
blind_name.why: A stone sarcophagus fills the foreground, with skeletal wall reliefs, cobwebs, and a burning torch behind it.
blind_name.odd: Deep shadows obscure some wall details.

notes.A: The side passage and yard are visible, but the near church wall cuts across them.
notes.B: The church corner and dirt path show through, but foreground foliage fills the frame.
notes.C: Two trees frame the path, but the low angle hides much of the church.
notes.D: The red sky silhouettes the courtyard trees, but the church is mostly out of view.
notes.E: The elevated view reveals the yard’s layout, but the path ends without a focal point.
notes.F: A bare tree marks the bend, but a close wall hides the path beyond.
notes.G: The skyline and far corner appear above a wall cap that blocks half the yard.
notes.H: The church wall and planting beds define the yard, but the blank façade dominates.

churchyard.best: E shows how the dirt path, sparse trees, enclosing walls, and church fit together beneath the city skyline.
churchyard.lacks: The churchyard has no visible graves or memorials. The path leads to a tree against a wall, leaving little to distinguish the yard from an empty garden.
churchyard.fix: Add a small burial plot at the end of the dirt path, with a tall weathered headstone visible from the entrance.

blind_name.name: Walled churchyard
blind_name.why: Weathered stone walls enclose a narrow dirt path and sparse trees beside a large stone building.
blind_name.odd: Deep shadows obscure the ground and the far end of the path.

notes.A: Street-level view gives the plaza depth, but the nearest entrance and sign are cropped.
notes.B: The canopy-top view shows the canyon between buildings, but hides the station entrances.
notes.C: A close view shows the timber-lined threshold, but the canopy hides much of the façade.
notes.D: Both entrances and the plaza read together, though the main passage fades into shadow.
notes.E: The raised side view shows the signs and canopies, but loses the plaza.
notes.F: The elevated view ties the plaza to the station, but crops the main entrance.
notes.G: Both entrances read clearly, but the foreground canopy dominates the view.
notes.H: The main doorway has depth, but the oversized foreground lamp steals attention.

station_front.best: D shows how the signed entrances, amber lamps, and looming façades frame the cobbled plaza.
station_front.lacks: A recognizable station entrance. The repeated timber openings blend into the block, leaving the green lettering to tell you what the building is.
station_front.fix: Rebuild the main entrance as a tall, illuminated portal with a staircase visibly descending from the plaza.

blind_name.name: Lamplit cobblestone courtyard
blind_name.why: Streetlamps line a paved courtyard enclosed by tall masonry buildings with wooden doors and open passages.
blind_name.odd: The right-hand passage fades into darkness.

notes.A: The elevated angle shows the carriage and tracks, but the blank wall dominates.
notes.B: The carriage roof fills the foreground and hides nearly everything that identifies the station.
notes.C: Tracks and waiting-room doors establish the layout, but the carriage reads as a slab.
notes.D: The clock, benches, and figure give the waiting room character, but the tracks disappear.
notes.E: Rails, carriage, and waiting room share the frame, though the far end recedes into murk.
notes.F: The rails and carriage lead into the scene, but the waiting room is cropped.
notes.G: The carriage windows and parallel tracks read clearly, but the waiting room barely registers.
notes.H: The curtained windows give the carriage character, but blank brick crowds out the railway context.

platform.best: E ties the tracks, green-striped carriage, and clock-lit waiting room together in one view.
platform.lacks: A clear boarding point. The waiting-room doors blend into the long brick wall, leaving the platform without a focal point.
platform.fix: Install a lit canopy over the waiting-room doors, casting light across the boarding strip and onto the carriage.

blind_name.name: Railway station platform
blind_name.why: Rails run beside a raised platform with a bench and wall clock.
blind_name.odd: Bright green strips under the platform look out of place.

notes.A: Shows the timetable and passage, but clips the station name and benches.
notes.B: The passage and timetable read clearly, but the head-on view flattens the hall.
notes.C: The station name and waiting area read together, though the passenger is clipped.
notes.D: Benches and columns establish the hall’s length, but the station details recede into darkness.
notes.E: The columns and benches explain the layout, but the signs are small and partly cropped.
notes.F: The posters, clock, and telephone read clearly, but the foreground bench overwhelms the frame.
notes.G: The bench leads toward the telephone and doorway, but the open side is barely visible.
notes.H: The side aisle and passenger are visible, but foreground columns hide most station details.

booking_hall.best: The station name, clock, telephone, posters, and passenger beside the bench give the waiting hall a distinct identity.
booking_hall.lacks: The hall lacks a recognizable service point. The benches show where to wait, but the room gives arriving travelers no obvious destination.
booking_hall.fix: Build a recessed, warmly lit ticket window beneath the arrivals and departures board.

blind_name.name: Waiting room
blind_name.why: A long wooden bench and wall clock suggest a waiting area beside an open doorway.
blind_name.odd: The small framed object beside the clock is hard to make out.

notes.A: The rail-lined quay leads into town, but the foreground pier dwarfs the distant barge.
notes.B: Crates and flag give the deck character, but the central mast splits the view.
notes.C: The broadside shows the hull clearly, but the cropped city leaves the barge isolated.
notes.D: The high angle clarifies the gap beside the quay, but the near hull runs offscreen.
notes.E: Hull, deck cargo and flag are legible, though the street disappears into shadow.
notes.F: The city frontage is clear, but a close crate hides most of the waterfront.
notes.G: The pier frames the city, but its pilings break up the view of the barge.
notes.H: Water and rooftops peek around a piling that dominates the frame.

harbour.place: City harbour with a cargo barge
harbour.best: E shows the barge’s hull, crates and skull flag beside the quay, with the city visible beyond.
harbour.lacks: The harbour lacks a distinctive vessel silhouette. The barge’s straight sides and flat deck make it easy to mistake for another pier.
harbour.fix: Reshape the existing barge with a tapered bow and a raised stern so its outline reads as a vessel from across the quay.

blind_name.name: Pirate ship at a harbor
blind_name.why: A skull flag flies above a wooden deck with cargo crates beside a stone quay.
blind_name.odd: The passage ahead is almost entirely black.

notes.A: The full counter and surrounding aisles read clearly, though the hanging cuts look small.
notes.B: The angle shows the aisle beside the counter, but a dark crate crowds the foreground.
notes.C: The counter leads into the hall, but the nearest carcass blocks much of the view.
notes.D: Lanterns and brick stalls frame the counter, but a giant foreground carcass dominates.
notes.E: Hanging cuts, jugs, and stocked shelves define the market, though the counter’s near end is cropped.
notes.F: The low aisle view shows the layout, but a shelf end hides much of the counter.
notes.G: The shelving dominates the aisle view, with the meat counter cut off at left.
notes.H: Lanterns and hanging cuts give the market character, but the tight crop obscures the layout.

market_hall.best: E shows the hanging cuts, lanterns, stocked shelves, and cluttered butcher’s counter together, with the aisle still visible.
market_hall.lacks: The hall lacks an architectural focal point. The flat ceiling and repeated shelves make its distinctive butcher’s counter feel incidental.
market_hall.fix: Build a timber-framed canopy over the butcher’s counter to give the hanging cuts a distinct stall and the hall a recognizable centerpiece.

blind_name.name: Butcher shop
blind_name.why: Large cuts of meat hang from the ceiling above a wooden counter.
blind_name.odd: nothing

notes.A: The bookshop peeks past a brick partition while a bright counter jar steals attention.
notes.B: The broad concourse connects several shops, but dim entrances and clipped lettering blur their identities.
notes.C: The clock shop’s sign and display shelves read clearly, but the arcade recedes into darkness.
notes.D: The clock and bookshop frame the concourse, though identical figures make the scene feel staged.
notes.E: The clock display and checkered shop floors are readable, but the head-on view flattens the arcade.
notes.F: Several shop bays and a robed figure establish the space, but the shop signs barely register.
notes.G: Brick jambs frame a robed figure and pottery, but conceal most of the storefronts.
notes.H: The tobacco counter and deep aisle give context, but the foreground figure dominates.

arcade.best: The clock, BOOKS sign, patterned concourse, and figures make the arcade and its shops legible in one glance.
arcade.lacks: The arcade lacks a focal point that ties its shops together. Repeated dark brick and similar openings make the storefronts run together.
arcade.fix: Install a tall, warmly lit freestanding clock in the concourse where shoppers can see it from several storefronts.

blind_name.name: Ornate hallway with library alcove
blind_name.why: A large wall clock overlooks patterned tiles beside an open room with bookshelves and candles.
blind_name.odd: The clock is partly cropped, and the book spines are too dark to read.

notes.A: Stage access, figures, and patterned carpet establish the lobby, though the signs recede into shadow.
notes.B: The ticket sign and show poster identify the theater, but a foreground post divides them from the room.
notes.C: The raised floor and stage access explain the layout, though a column interrupts the view.
notes.D: Figures gather near the manager’s door, but the patterned overhang dominates the frame.
notes.E: A post and raised ledge show the construction, but the tight framing hides the lobby.
notes.F: The manager’s office and stage door read clearly, but the cropped figure crowds the foreground.
notes.G: The long view shows the lobby’s depth, but the foreground figure steals attention.
notes.H: Tickets and a show poster identify the lobby, but the low ceiling overwhelms them.

auditorium.best: A frames the stage door, costumed figures, and ornate lobby trim together, with enough floor visible to show their relationship.
auditorium.lacks: The lobby lacks a dominant architectural feature that tells visitors where the show is. Small signs carry that information against walls of equally busy ornament.
auditorium.fix: Turn a stretch of patterned wall into a recessed auditorium entrance with a lit marquee visible across the lobby.

blind_name.name: Ornate theater auditorium
blind_name.why: Patterned carpeting, ornate wall trim, a raised platform, and an exit sign suggest a theater.
blind_name.odd: The dark left wall and doorway obscure interior details.

notes.A: Tables and figures peek past a close wall that swallows half the view.
notes.B: Shows the seating layout clearly, but the bare foreground makes the room feel sparse.
notes.C: The full whiskey sign sets the scene, but the boxy partition dominates.
notes.D: The diagonal counter displays the bottles well, but the high angle hides most seating.
notes.E: Close bottles and the whiskey sign establish the saloon, but the blank corner draws attention.
notes.F: Counter, stools and figures give the room character, though the sign is clipped.
notes.G: Paintings and a barred window add character, but the near wall crowds the view.
notes.H: The aisle shows the counter and tables, but a tall chair blocks the far wall.

saloon.best: The long counter leads past bottles, stools and figures to the whiskey sign, showing how the saloon fits together.
saloon.lacks: The counters, tables and walls blend into the same dark wood tones. The saloon lacks a focal point that makes it clear where drinks are served.
saloon.fix: Build a warmly lit backbar with tiered bottle shelves behind the main counter.

blind_name.name: Wood-paneled saloon
blind_name.why: A long wooden bar, bottles, stemmed glasses, and red-topped stools fill the room.
blind_name.odd: The tall chair backs look like tangled metal grilles.

notes.A: Pottery and the barred hatch read clearly, but the pawn counter is out of frame.
notes.B: The display ledge leads past LOANS, but the back door becomes the focus.
notes.C: The skeleton by the counter adds character, but the opposite facade dominates.
notes.D: Window goods lead into the shop, though the dark mullion interrupts the view.
notes.E: The clothes and PAWN counter read clearly, but the storefront's street context disappears.
notes.F: The display ledge and checkerboard floor frame a door that tells little about the shop.
notes.G: Goblets, candle, and pitcher line the window, but the street wall overwhelms them.
notes.H: The pitcher and crate have presence, but the heavy door crowds out the shop's identity.

pawn.best: The street-side view frames the pawn counter, loan sign, hanging clothes, and window goods together.
pawn.lacks: The pawn counter has little visual pull. The flat lighting gives the merchandise, checkerboard floor, and back door nearly equal weight.
pawn.fix: Add a warm pool of light over the pawn counter so the goods and transaction area draw the eye from the street.

blind_name.name: Pawn shop window display
blind_name.why: A glass storefront displays hanging shirts, pottery, candles, and goblets beside a wooden counter.
blind_name.odd: The far-right edge is too dark to make out.

notes.A: The sludge pit and raised grating establish two levels, but columns break up the view.
notes.B: The FILTER sign, vat and controls establish purpose, but close walls squeeze them together.
notes.C: The grated lane and SLUDGE lettering give context, but the low beam hides the hall.
notes.D: The raised grating and tall striped panel suggest scale, but columns obscure the machinery.
notes.E: The wide grating and overhead structures show the layout, but the vats blend into shadow.
notes.F: The SLUDGE sign and orange console frame the grating, but the sludge itself stays hidden.
notes.G: Sludge, controls and grating share the frame, but the central column splits the view.
notes.H: The striped overhang frames the grate and cropped sign, but the view ends at steelwork.

machine_hall.best: The green sludge, orange controls and grated walkway together make the hall read as a working plant.
machine_hall.lacks: A recognizable piece of machinery that connects the sludge vats to the controls and shows what the hall does.
machine_hall.fix: Install a large sludge filter above the vats, with exposed pipes that visibly feed into them.

blind_name.name: Industrial machine hall
blind_name.why: Rusted steel walls, hazard stripes, and a control panel surround a channel of green liquid.
blind_name.odd: The central pillar blocks much of the view, and the control panel markings are unreadable.

notes.A: Green runoff leads toward a distant torch, but repeating wall panels flatten the view.
notes.B: A masonry block fills the passage and hides most of the sewer.
notes.C: Wall growth and scattered debris make the tunnel feel damp and neglected. The fan recedes.
notes.D: The channel marks a junction, but identical walls make both routes look interchangeable.
notes.E: A red canister punctuates a recessed bay whose empty floor dominates the shot.
notes.F: A torch picks out a stained corner, with the channel barely visible below.
notes.G: The fan and creature frame the runoff, but the far end dissolves into darkness.
notes.H: A broad pool wraps around the corner, dwarfing the creature and distant masonry block.

sewer.best: The overhead fan, green runoff, and ratlike creature give the tunnel a function, an atmosphere, and a sense of scale.
sewer.lacks: The sewer lacks a spatial focal point. The same low ceiling and wall panels repeat, and the channel has no visible destination.
sewer.fix: Turn one junction into a tall outfall chamber where the channel drops into a catch basin.

blind_name.name: Industrial sewer corridor
blind_name.why: Rusted metal walls, a ceiling grate, and a green channel run along a narrow passage.
blind_name.odd: The far end is too dark to make out clearly.

notes.A: Shows the stair flight and upper landing, but the wall reduces the concourse to a sliver.
notes.B: Shows the turn and rising steps, but deep shadow flattens the landing.
notes.C: Shows the EXIT sign and barred booth clearly, but clips most of the stair flight.
notes.D: Shows the concourse leading into the underpass, but leaves the ticket booth out of view.
notes.E: Frames the red-tiled entrance and EXIT sign, but the stair turn disappears behind the jamb.
notes.F: Catches the stairs and ticket sign, but the foreground wall breaks their connection.
notes.G: Gives the clearest view of the ticket grille, but the foreground pillar hides the stairs.
notes.H: Connects the stairs and ticket concourse, but the booth recedes into murk.

underpass.best: H shows how the red-tiled stairs, EXIT sign, and barred ticket booth fit together under one low ceiling.
underpass.lacks: The junction lacks a strong focal point. The ticket grille and signs suggest a station, but the booth blends into the masonry.
underpass.fix: Rebuild the barred recess as a warmly lit ticket booth with a service counter visible from the foot of the stairs.

blind_name.name: Stone underpass
blind_name.why: A low stone ceiling covers a tiled passage with stairs on the left and a barred gate on the right.
blind_name.odd: Deep shadows obscure details on the stairs and beyond the gate.

notes.A: The long approach reveals the shop, but a stone pier takes up half the frame.
notes.B: A lamppost anchors the corner but blocks the view toward the passage.
notes.C: The close-up reveals the counter and checkerboard floor, but crops away almost the entire yard.
notes.D: The passage, tables, and lamppost map the courtyard clearly, but the shop is distant.
notes.E: The high angle shows the route around the pier, which dominates the right half.
notes.F: Tables, figures, and the shop animate the yard, but repetitive brick fills the background.
notes.G: The full sign and serving hatch identify the shop, but little of the yard appears.
notes.H: A clear storefront view reveals food at the hatch, but leaves the courtyard out.

works_yard.best: F puts the serving hatch, tables, lamppost, and robed figures in one view, with room to read the courtyard.
works_yard.lacks: The courtyard lacks a strong focal point. The serving hatch is its most distinctive feature, yet it reads as another opening in a wall of repeating windows.
works_yard.fix: Extend the Rat Dogs serving hatch into the courtyard as a roofed service counter that the tables can cluster around.

blind_name.name: Brick courtyard with streetlamp
blind_name.why: A lit streetlamp stands on dark paving beside café tables and tall windowed walls.
blind_name.odd: The leftmost table is cropped, and the dark windows reveal no interiors.

notes.A: The aisle shows both prep counters, but the rats and cleaver recede into shadow.
notes.B: A rat fills the foreground against the kitchen shelves, but the near wall crowds it.
notes.C: The steel table makes the rats unmistakable, but the tight angle hides the diner seating.
notes.D: The aisle and stocked shelf show the layout, but the near wall dominates.
notes.E: Stools and the long counter suggest a diner, but the blank wall commands the frame.
notes.F: Foreground rats and a figure in the alley add intrigue, but the bare wall dominates.
notes.G: The cleaver, rats, and pans sell the kitchen, though the foreground counter hides most seating.
notes.H: Stools, counters, and fixtures explain the room, but the rats get lost in the wide view.

ratdogs.best: The cleaver and rats tell the story up front, with steel prep tables, hanging pans, and stools establishing the diner.
ratdogs.lacks: A recognizable cooking station. The rats and cleaver tell us what gets prepped, but the room gives that joke nowhere to go.
ratdogs.fix: Install a lit industrial griddle against the back wall, with a row of rats sizzling beneath its hood.

blind_name.name: Rat-infested kitchen
blind_name.why: Hanging pans, metal prep counters, and a large blade suggest a kitchen.
blind_name.odd: Rat-like creatures are scattered across the work surfaces.
